prompt: Produce exactly one concise caption (one sentence) that states only visually verifiable facts. The caption MUST contain 2–6 discrete facts (clauses) in a single sentence separated by semicolons; define a “fact” as one clause drawn from the prioritized checklist below and include items in this priority order when they are visibly present: 1) legible text (transcribe exact characters in single quotes and give approximate placement, e.g., "Sign reads 'DUNG ANH' on riverbank"); 2) numeric counts and canonical object types (use digits, e.g., "2 people", "1 bicycle"); 3) one discriminative attribute per counted object when visible (color, material, pattern, logo/text, or a visible part, e.g., "red plastic basin", "blue Mets jersey with orange script", "handlebars"); 4) pose/action/orientation for people or animals if clearly visible (one concise verb phrase, e.g., "standing and speaking", "mid-jump with bent knees", "looking toward camera"); 5) simple spatial layout using foreground/midground/background or left/right relations; 6) lighting, viewpoint, or occlusion cues if present (e.g., "bright sunlight casting long shadows", "viewed through glass with reflections", "foreground foliage partially obscures table"). Rules and format requirements: do not infer roles, emotions, intentions, metaphors, slogans, or marketing language; do not use vague quantifiers such as "several," "many," or "a group of" — use digits or omit; transcribe text only if clearly legible (if only partial, label it explicitly as partial, e.g., "partial text: 'AMER...'"); use canonical object names (e.g., "chain-link fence," "wooden skiff," "ride-on motorcycle") and include one visible part detail when available; each counted object mentioned MUST include at least one visible attribute if visible; keep the caption compact and factual (no lists, tags, JSON, extra sentences, or commentary). Before returning the caption, apply this internal checklist: A) was any clearly legible text transcribed and placed? B) are numeric counts included for visible instances? C) does each counted object have ≥1 visible attribute? D) are visible people given a pose/action/gaze clause? E) are visible occlusion/reflection/layering cues noted? If any checklist item applies to the image but is missing from the caption, regenerate once automatically to include the missing required items; then return the single final sentence with 2–6 facts only.
